description.text:
The prize cards of BattleZone, the organized play Wizards of the Coast ran from November 2002 in its last year with the Pokémon license. Stores ran it as a weekly league or a monthly tournament, with a prize kit for each season: 16 Classic promos, eight Best of Game cards with a gold foil Winner stamp, and one jumbo Winner card, which is not holo and has its stamp printed. In a tournament the stamped cards went to the top four players and the head judge; in a league the season's best players each got one, and the top one to four players the jumbo. Each season had a Best of Game card of its own, and its unstamped copy came back a few months later as a later season's Classic promo.

Wizards lost the license before the June and July 2003 seasons were played. Their tournament kits had gone out, but not their league kits, so Rocket's Mewtwo and Rocket's Hitmonchan exist only with the Winner stamp and as jumbos. Professor Elm, given out at Gen Con 2003, has no Winner or jumbo version. Electabuzz, Hitmonchan, Professor Elm, Rocket's Mewtwo and Rocket's Hitmonchan are reverse holo; Rocket's Scizor, Rocket's Sneasel, Dark Ivysaur and Dark Venusaur are not.

tell.text: A foil "winner" stamp on the picture: lowercase with a star on Wizards of the Coast cards, "WINNER" beside a Poké Ball on later ones. No foil anywhere on the card. An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.

description.text: A jumbo copy of the Winner card, one in each BattleZone prize kit of the November and December 2002 season, for one of the season's top players. It is non-holo all over, its gold Winner stamp simply printed. BattleZone was the last year of Wizards of the Coast's Pokémon League. The top 16 at each Super BattleZone tournament of 24 and 25 May 2003 got one too.
